newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pro7 boosts ad revs in first half of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pro7 boosts ad revs in first half of 1997.

text.p: Germany's Pro Sieben Media AG television group said on Monday that advertising revenues rose some 21.2 percent to 1.55 billion marks ($867.1 million) in the first six months of 1997 from the same period a year earlier.

The company said that based on data collected by the research group Nielsen S+P, German subisidiary of the Dunn and Bradstreet company, Pro Sieben's share of the TV advertising market was 27 percent at the end of June, up from 24 percent a year ago. ($ = 1.787 German Marks)
Pro7 boosts ad revs in first half of =2

Pro Sieben, which was listed on the stock exchange earlier this month, said gross advertising revenues were expanding much faster than the broader market. Net advertising revenues -- adjusted to exclude discounts and agency commissions -- are around 30-40 percent lower, Pro Sieben said.
During the first half of the year, television gross advertising revenues rose 8.7 percent to 5.8 billion marks.
The company's two television stations -- Pro Sieben and Kabel 1 -- both posted advertising gains in the first half.
The Pro Sieben channel saw gross advertising revenues rise 18.5 percent to 1.33 billion marks, while Kabel 1 revenues surged 46.3 percent to 222 million marks.
"We are more than satisfied with the turnover development at Pro Sieben and Kabel 1 in the first half of 1997," said Michael Woelfle, the company's marketing director.
"We also expect growth rates for the full year that are clearly above the market average," he added.
The company added that it would probably present detailed figures on business in the first half of the year in September.
